page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v6 is an x86_64 compute instance from the Dlsv6 series, configured for compute-dense workloads requiring reduced memory allocations per vCPU. The server is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at up to 4.2 GHz, providing 48 physical cores and 96 virtual CPUs via hyperthreading. Hardware resources include 192 GB of total memory, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 vector acceleration. This instance does not include local disk storage or discrete GPUs, relying entirely on remote network-attached storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate significant compute capacity across multi-threaded applications. The instance achieved top-tier ratings in PassMark CPU score (86191.93) and Geekbench multi-core performance (21482.0), driven by its high core density and vector capabilities. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 509.95 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measured 115.45 GB/sec. Memory benchmarks register 257.01 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 107.31 GB/sec for write throughput. In machine learning inference evaluations using small and medium models, CPU prompt processing showed strong results, reaching 3092.62 tokens/sec on a 135M model and 275.37 tokens/sec on a 7B model.

By provisioning 2 GB of RAM per vCPU, the D96ls_v6 delivers cost-effective compute scaling for tasks that do not exhaust large memory allocations. It is well suited for CPU-bound distributed workloads, large-scale CI/CD build pipelines, batch transcoding, web service aggregation, and CPU-based machine learning inference. Workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets or low-latency ephemeral local storage must leverage alternative instance tiers or provision external storage volumes.

It features no local disk storage and zero discrete GPUs, relying on remote volumes for persistent data. In benchmark testing, the platform exhibits high-tier multi-threaded processing, scoring 86191.93 in PassMark CPU and delivering 115.45 GB/sec in static web throughput. This architecture provides an efficient allocation for high-concurrency tasks where memory density is secondary to raw CPU throughput, such as large-scale compilation, batch compute processing, microservices hosting, and lightweight model inference.
